summary: We are testing whether spatially-intelligent 2-opt moves (using a grid-based neighbor lookup) can improve TSP tour quality beyond the 69.5 score achieved in iteration 2's random-swap + boundary 2-opt approach. A single experiment arm implements a two-phase simulated annealing strategy: Phase 1 (0–1.3s) uses grid-guided 2-opt with stale position tracking for broad exploration, Phase 2 (1.3–1.85s) uses exact position tracking with short segments (≤20) for precise refinement.
key_points: Testing one arm (h-main): grid-guided 2-opt SA replacing iter-2's random 2-opt, predicted to score above 71.0 vs iter-2's 69.5 baseline

Core mechanism: a sqrt(N)-sized grid partitions cities spatially, enabling O(1) lookup of nearby cities as 2-opt reversal partners — this should find edge-uncrossing opportunities that random selection misses

Two-phase design: Phase 1 allows unlimited segment reversals with periodic pos[] rebuild (batch=300) for exploration; Phase 2 restricts to segments ≤20 with per-move pos[] update for precise local optimization

Confirmation criterion: measured judge score consistently above 71.0; refutation if score ≤ 69.5, which would indicate grid-guided candidates aren't producing accepted moves or pos[] staleness is harmful
Key diagnostic: if score doesn't improve, check (1) acceptance rate of grid-guided 2-opt moves, (2) pos[] accuracy drift in Phase 1, (3) whether Phase 1→Phase 2 transition degrades quality
Time budget: 2s per test case; phases end at 1.3s and 1.85s respectively, leaving margin; judge call expected ~45s wall time
